sources.title: Mars 2020 Science Investigation CTX DEM Mosaic
sources.provider: USGS Astrogeology Science Center / NASA PDS (primary author Fred Calef)
sources.license: Product page: Use Constraints 'public domain'; Access Constraints 'please cite authors'
sources.horizontal_units: metres (map metres; true ground scale only at lat_ts 18.4663 N, corrected per row)
sources.vertical_units: metres (product page: Vertical Coordinate System Units = Meters; vertically localized to MOLA)
sources.used_for: Slope and passability (routing), elevation along route, hillshade base layer
sources.caveats: Product page lists Radius A/C = 3396160 m while the GeoTIFF CRS states R = 3396190 m; georeferencing uses the file CRS. A previous measurement in this folder (veri/egim_esik_olcumu.json) found that 20 m CTX slopes miss many steep features that HiRISE 1 m slopes resolve (only 26.2% recall of HiRISE p90 > 20 deg cells at a 20 deg CTX threshold).

sources.title: Mars 2020 Terrain Relative Navigation HiRISE DTM Mosaic
sources.provider: USGS Astrogeology Science Center (Fergason, R. L., Hare, T. M., Mayer, D. P., et al., 2020); HiRISE: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona
sources.license: Product page: Access Constraints 'None'; Use Constraints 'Please cite authors'
sources.coverage_lonlat: 77.2229-77.584 E, 18.3068-18.6693 N (product page and file bounds agree); ~66% of the raster has valid data
sources.horizontal_units: metres (map metres; lat_ts = 0, so east-west ground spacing = 1 m * cos(lat), corrected per row)
sources.vertical_units: metres (product page: Vertical Coordinate System Units = Meters)
sources.used_for: 1 m slope statistics per 60 m routing cell inside its footprint (p90 for passability, mean for reporting). Cells need >= 90% valid 1 m slopes.
sources.alignment_check: Pixel centres mapped exactly via the shared sphere (x_ctx = x_hirise * cos(18.4663 deg)); HiRISE vs CTX cell mean-slope correlation 0.852 at zero offset, lower at +-1 or +-3 cell shifts.
